t: You're looking at numbers 39 to 46 Connaught Square, a group of buildings in Westminster. They were designed by George Gutch, a British architect and surveyor who was born in 1790. Gutch served four successive Bishops of London as surveyor for much of the Diocese's southern strip of the parish of Paddington, roughly five hundred acres. That is why his name turns up here. The square was part of land held by the Bishops, and Gutch was the man looking after it on their behalf.
